meta.name: Latch — clear the retired policy-timelock nominations; the Safe stays owner
meta.description: Safe nonce SECOND. The Policy tier no longer exists; the four contracts nominated to the RETIRED policy timelock 0x1Da3AD33 stay with the Safe, per CLAUDE.md's ownership table. Four cancel() calls kill the retired timelock's queued acceptOwnership operations, which have been READY — executable by anyone — since 1789150854. Four transferOwnership(Safe)+acceptOwnership() pairs overwrite and then clear each stale pendingOwner, leaving owner=Safe, pendingOwner=0. One schedule() on the retired policy timelock queues CLPositionDescriptor.transferOwnership(Safe) at the 6h minimum delay: the descriptor is plain Ownable and the earlier batch handed it to the retired policy timelock outright, so the only way back is through that timelock's own queue. GRIEFABLE UNTIL IT LANDS: if a stranger executes any of the four ready operations first, that contract's owner becomes the retired timelock, its transferOwnership(Safe) here reverts, and the whole batch fails with GS013. Re-read owner() on all four and isOperationDone on all four ids immediately before signing; if any has flipped, do not submit — see the fallback in README.md.

_notes.second_step_after_6h: Permissionless. Anyone calls execute(CLPositionDescriptor, 0, transferOwnership(Safe), 0x0, salt) on 0x1Da3AD33AB8151Af9EE91b90fA23fFdDFf9C0C3A. Exact calldata in README.md.
_notes.why_not_transferOwnership_zero: Ownable2Step.transferOwnership has no zero check, so transferOwnership(address(0)) would clear each nomination in one call. It is not used because a 'transfer to zero' in a signing UI is indistinguishable at a glance from a renounce, which CLAUDE.md tells signers to reject on sight. Two explicit calls whose end state is owner=Safe, pendingOwner=0 are worth the extra gas.
